#1 Has anyone seen this notion in print? The idea is to capture examples of bicategories like CoSpan\mathrm{CoSpan}CoSpan, CoRel\mathrm{CoRel}CoRel, etc.

Here is how one might define cocartesian bicategories, by adapting the development in cartesian bicategory. Following Carboni and Walters, a left adjoint in a bicategory is called a map. Pseudofunctors between bicategories are called homomorphisms. By “transformation”, I mean what Bénabou calls an “oplax transformation” and what Johnstone calls a “lax transformation”. A transformation is strong if its structural 2-cells are invertible. A transformation θ:F→G\theta: F \to Gθ:F→G between homomorphisms B→C\mathbf{B} \to \mathbf{C}B→C is map-valued if θb:Fb→Gb\theta b: F b \to G bθb:Fb→Gb is a map in C\mathbf{C}C for every object bbb of B\mathbf{B}B.

A cocartesian bicategory is a bicategory B\mathbf{B}B equipped with

  • Homomorphisms ⊕:B×B→B,E:1→B\oplus: \mathbf{B} \times \mathbf{B} \to \mathbf{B}, E: \mathbf{1} \to \mathbf{B}⊕:B×B→B,E:1→B where 1\mathbf{1}1 is the terminal bicategory,

  • Map-valued transformations

  • ∇:⊕Δ→1B\nabla: \oplus \Delta \to 1_\mathbf{B}∇:⊕Δ→1B​,
  • ι:1B×B→Δ⊕\iota: 1_{\mathbf{B} \times \mathbf{B}} \to \Delta \oplusι:1B×B​→Δ⊕,
  • η:E!→1B\eta: E ! \to 1_\mathbf{B}η:E!→1B​,

where Δ:B→B×B\Delta: \mathbf{B} \to \mathbf{B} \times \mathbf{B}Δ:B→B×B is the diagonal homomorphism and !:B→1!: \mathbf{B} \to \mathbf{1}!:B→1 is the unique homomorphism,

  • Invertible modifications

E\\ \mathllap{1_{\oplus}} \downarrow & \overset{s}{\Rightarrow} & \downarrow \mathrlap{\nabla \oplus} & & & & \mathllap{1_{\Delta}} \downarrow & \overset{t}{\Leftarrow} & \downarrow \mathrlap{\Delta \nabla} & & & & \mathllap{1_{E}} \downarrow & \overset{u}{\Rightarrow} & \downarrow \mathrlap{\eta E}\\ \oplus & \underset{1_{\oplus}}{\to} & \oplus & & & & \Delta & \underset{1_{\Delta}}{\to} & \Delta & & & & I & \underset{1_E}{\to} & E \end{matrix}⊕1⊕​↓⊕​→⊕ι⇒s1⊕​→​​⊕Δ⊕↓∇⊕⊕​​​​Δ1Δ​↓Δ​→ιΔ⇐t1Δ​→​​Δ⊕Δ↓Δ∇Δ​​​​E1E​↓I​→E⋅11​⇒u1E​→​​E!E↓ηEE​

satisfying appropriate triangulator (“swallowtail”) coherence conditions.

As ever, there is a lemma that states that if θ\thetaθ is a transformation and fff is a map, then the structural 2-cell θ⋅f\theta \cdot fθ⋅f is an isomorphism. Then, the data above restrict to the bicategory Map(B)\mathrm{Map}(\mathbf{B})Map(B) whose 1-cells are maps in B\mathbf{B}B, so that ∇,ι,η\nabla, \iota, \eta∇,ι,η restrict to strong transformations and ⊕\oplus⊕ becomes a left biadjoint to Δ\DeltaΔ, i.e., a 2-coproduct, and EEE becomes 2-initial (EEE is for “empty”). The development then proceeds much as it does on the cartesian bicategory page.

Unless I am pretty confused, this notion does not seem to be a simple “co” dual of the notion of cartesian bicategory. For example, these are not co-map valued transformations, and the transformations are still Johnstone-lax, but we are changing directions on the transformations appropriately to get codiagonals and coprojections when we restrict to Map(B)\mathrm{Map}(\mathbf{B})Map(B) (which will be Set\mathrm{Set}Set in the examples CoSpan\mathrm{CoSpan}CoSpan and CoRel\mathrm{CoRel}CoRel).
